title: Revising a project memory does not require resending its whole body
outcome: Revising a project memory does not require resending its whole body
acceptance: A whole-body revise keeps working unchanged
The receipt shows what changed relative to the previous revision (a bounded diff or the changed section), so the writer can confirm nothing was dropped

remember --revise can change part of a memory (append a paragraph, or replace one marked section) without resending the unchanged body, keeping the expected-revision conflict check and attributed revision history

completion.summary:
A project memory can be revised in part. With --revise, --key and --expected-revision N, `--append` adds a paragraph and `--section NAME` replaces the interior of one section marked `<!-- engram-section NAME -->` … `<!-- /engram-section NAME -->` (MCP append/section).

The body is built from revision N inside the writer transaction, keeping every other byte, so an exact retry replays and a stale basis conflicts. A missing section refuses with memory_section_not_found, naming the sections there are. Names are 1 to 64 bytes and never echoed. Empty text clears a section. Whole-body revise stores as before.

Every revise receipt shows the changed span as bounded excerpts, plus full reads of both revisions. History, replay and forget are unchanged.
